locator: Section 1 'Distribution System' note on inadequate pressure; Section 3 'Monthly Withdrawals & Purchases', December; Section 5, 2022 column
shows: Asheville's 2022 plan reports that from December 22 to 27, 2022, extreme cold affected the Mills River plant and the distribution system. Frozen coagulant lines took the Mills River plant offline for 3 days. In that time 27 breaks occurred in the distribution system, which stressed the other two plants; the demand from these breaks and from many private line breaks drained the storage tanks. The southern district, which Mills River supplies, and parts of the western district were without water for 5 to 8 days. The December maximum day use was 29.01 million gallons a day (December average 23.57); the 2022 total demand was 23.5815.
limits: Self-reported by the water system; the plan says that DWR staff do not field verify the data. The 29.01 million gallons a day is a production peak driven by breaks and refilling in a freeze, not customer use on a normal peak day. The plan does not give the date of the maximum day within December.

outage_days.note: Printed: Section 1 note, 'without water for 5-8 days'; the upper end of the range.

valid_for.place: City of Asheville water system (01-11-010); southern and parts of western districts

quotes.text: From December 22, 2022 - December 27, 2022 extreme cold weather temperatures occurred in the region which affected the Mills River and water distribution system.
The plant had to be temporarily offline (3 days) to replace frozen lines and repair other equipment that malfunctioned during the extreme temperatures.
During that time 27 breaks occurred in the distribution system which stressed the other two treatment plants.
The demand from these breaks and numerous private line breaks drained storage tanks in the distribution system.
All of the southern district supplied by Mills River and parts of the western district were without water for 5-8 days
Total Demand (MGD) 23.5815

locator: Section 3 'Monthly Withdrawals & Purchases'; Section 5 'Demand v/s Percent of Supply', 2025 column
shows: The City of Asheville's 2025 plan gives, for each month, the average daily use and the maximum day use. The highest maximum day of 2025 is 26.48 million gallons a day, in January (average daily use 24.05 that month); the lowest monthly maximum is 23.22 in March. Section 5 gives a 2025 service area demand of 21.4912 million gallons a day, sales of 1.1632 and a total demand of 22.6544. The ratio of the highest day to the total demand is 1.1689 (derived).
limits: Self-reported by the water system; the plan says that DWR staff do not field verify the data. One calendar year: the plan for 2022 reports a higher maximum day, during a freeze with many main breaks (related claim). The monthly figures are withdrawals and purchases, so they include the water sold to other systems, process water and losses (unaccounted-for water 5.4925 million gallons a day in 2025).

locator: Section 3 'Water Treatment Plants' and the questions under it; Section 5 notes
shows: Asheville's three water treatment plants have permitted capacities of 7.5 (Mills River WTP, Mills and French Broad rivers), 31.5 (North Fork WTP, Burnett Reservoir) and 5.0 (William DeBruhl WTP, Bee Tree Reservoir) million gallons a day: 44.0 in all (derived). Average daily production did not exceed 80% of approved plant capacity for five consecutive days in 2025. The system expects peak day demands to exceed the plant capacity within 10 years; phase 2 of the Mills River plant expansion is due by the end of 2027.
limits: Self-reported by the water system; the plan says that DWR staff do not field verify the data. Permitted capacities, not tested output. The plan states that the North Fork and William DeBruhl plants use direct filtration. The available raw surface water supply is 53.7 million gallons a day, more than the plant capacity.

shows: Asheville reports a finished water storage capacity of 27.3560 million gallons in its 2025 plan, for a system of about 1,274 miles of lines in 55 pressure zones. Its off-stream raw water storage is a separate 15 million gallons.
limits: Self-reported by the water system; the plan says that DWR staff do not field verify the data. Nominal capacity, not the volume that can be drawn. The figure predates the additional 1 million gallon clearwell of the Mills River expansion (phase 2, due by the end of 2027). The raw water storage is not finished water.
